gaps.sentence: ___ at this old photo — isn't it amazing?
gaps.explanation: 'Look at' means to direct your eyes towards something; the other verbs cannot be followed by 'at' here.

gaps.sentence: There is little ___ that the plan will be approved.
gaps.hint: pattern: little ___ that something will happen
gaps.explanation: 'Possibility that ...' is the standard pattern; 'opportunity' means a situation that lets you do something.

gaps.sentence: The money was divided ___ the four children.
gaps.hint: for a group of more than two
gaps.explanation: 'Among' is traditionally used for more than two; 'between' is preferred for exactly two.

gaps.sentence: She has had a brilliant ___ in politics.
gaps.hint: the whole course of a person's professional life
gaps.explanation: 'Career' is the progress through a working life, especially in one profession; 'job' is one position.

gaps.sentence: I was so ___ when I forgot her name in front of everyone.
gaps.hint: how you feel in an awkward social situation
gaps.explanation: 'Embarrassed' describes short-term discomfort in a social situation; 'ashamed' implies guilt about wrongdoing.

gaps.sentence: The company has changed ___ logo twice.
gaps.explanation: 'Its' is the possessive form of 'it'; 'it's' means 'it is' or 'it has'. 'Its'' does not exist.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her presentation and her handling of questions.
All ___ must wear identity badges at all times on site.
gaps.explanation: 'Personnel' = the employees of an organisation; 'personal' is an adjective.
